_comment: Configuration for scripts/run_ratchets.py (spec S15.3-S15.7).
WHAT A GATE MAY CHECK. A property of the code that is either true or false,
and whose false case a reviewer would independently call a defect: the
dependency graph points one way, a declared symbol is used, both sides of the
protocol come from one schema, a tool description names tools that exist, a
corrective changes state rather than composing a sentence.
WHAT A GATE MAY NOT CHECK. A number standing in for a judgement. The size
gate that used to live here capped files at 800 lines, functions at 80 and
nesting at 3, and what it actually produced was code shaped to satisfy it:
an API that swallowed its own error to save a line, files split on length
rather than responsibility, and a sidecar sitting at exactly 800/800. Good
design is enforced by review and by the property gates below, not by a
budget. Removed 2026-08-02; do not reintroduce it in another form.
Every gate declares whether it is LIVE. A live gate must find at least
min_subjects things to inspect; a dormant gate must find exactly zero. That
second half is the important one: it means the day phase 4 lands a tool
registry, the tool-honesty gate stops being dormant BY FAILING, and someone
has to flip live:true deliberately. A dormant gate that silently reports
green is v1's `ctest -E realmodel` -- a selector that matched nothing while
printing a number that looked fine.
Exemptions are by path, and every one carries a reason. There is no
wildcard-with-no-explanation entry, and adding one should be as awkward as
it looks.

scan_exempt.reason: Ported verbatim from v1 (S18). These are the falsifiers, and an entrant edited to satisfy anything is no longer the thing that was measured.

The consolidated blast-radius engine, ported from v1 unmodified. It is graded by bakeoff/blast_radius (0 wmiss corpus, 15 wmiss holdout, re-measured 2026-07-30 in this repo) and the e00_merged scoreboard includes THIS header, so editing it detaches the measured number from the shipped code. If it is ever rewritten, the rewrite must be re-scored first.
Cook-off-merged edit engine ported from v1 unmodified, so a verbatim upstream fix can land without a gate arguing with it. Same measured-evidence argument as blast_radius.hpp.

dead_code_exempt.reason: The production Clock. Referenced only from main() in the sidecar, which does not exist until phase 4; tests use ManualClock. Remove this entry when the sidecar lands.
The replay side of the byte-faithful trace pair (S2.1.4). Its only non-test caller is ReplayBackend, phase 2. Kept because shipping an encoder with no decoder is how a trace stops being replayable.

Request payload types are the WIRE CONTRACT, consumed by the TypeScript client (extension/src/client.ts) and regenerated + diffed by the protocol gate. The sidecar reads request fields by name off the framed message rather than deserializing a struct, so the C++ mirror is unreferenced by construction. Deleting it would break the one-schema-two-sides property S4.4 exists for.
